# Unsupported vmangos behavior

This list covers the ported Import Families. The family imports and generated censuses report
these Compatibility Manifest findings. The vmangos Source Profile now checks consumed columns and approved source values. Counts do not gate import.

| Finding | Selected rows | Current limit | Next slice |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `globals.portal-condition` | 16 | `areatrigger_teleport.required_condition` is nonzero, but the Module's portal catalogue has no condition field. The current classic-db import also omits portal conditions. The globals import retains these rows and reports their trigger ids as unsupported. | S3g translates condition kinds. Portal gameplay support remains unimplemented. |

Verified against vmangos commit `464179081673cfd240f7ffe7f0daf96bca0b5a70`, selected for patch 10,
and the current `build_areatrigger_teleport_sql` output columns. No source rows are included here.

Items findings count emitted offers, keyed by creature and item. Full-world has 403 runtime-conditioned
offers, 208 offers with item flags, and 951 offers with a restock interval. Alliance-single has
21, 36 and 276 respectively. The Module stores `max_count`, but no restock interval, source item
flags or offer condition. The items import retains the offers and reports these fields as
`items.vendor-condition`, `items.vendor-item-flags` and `items.vendor-restock`. The generated
items censuses include these counts. The loot audit below includes source conditions. The 16 portal conditions above remain unsupported.

The loot audit covers all nine selected source tables, before profile-specific owner filtering.
These counts are source rows after patch and static-condition selection.
The items manifest also reports findings from creature and reference loot. Quest mail uses the
single-item, unconditional validation added in S3f.

| Finding | Occurrences | Current limit |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `loot.condition` | 4085 | The loot tables have no runtime condition field. Static WOW_PATCH conditions are applied before expansion. |
| `loot.count-range` | 5960 | The current import stores the maximum count. |
| `loot.quest-only` | 35 | Fishing and skinning tables have no quest-only flag. |
| `loot.unconsumed-table` | 2741 | Item-container and disenchant source tables have no world import path. |

The generated loot censuses break these findings down by source table. Item-container loot has
2,660 selected rows and disenchant loot has 81. The 16 portal conditions remain unsupported.

The pre-existing small-chance clamp remains. A positive independent chance below one basis point
can emit one basis point. Fishing and skinning quest-only flags remain unsupported.

conditions remain unsupported. Compiling patch predicates and owning condition kinds does not
add a condition field to the portal catalogue. Untranslated script dispatch remains unsupported. The Source Profile gate is implemented.

Nested pools with unequal child limits remain inactive with their definitions and placements retained. The five unplaced level-zero templates have no defined class-level stat lookup and are omitted. The cast model keeps the first spell and an existing secondary rotation; source slot probabilities, target parameters, flags, initial/repeat delays and scripts remain unsupported. Formations and scheduled game events have no runtime. Waypoint orientation, delay, wander radius and scripts remain unrepresented, as do alternate paths. Spawn resource percentages, respawn ranges, active/random flags and per-spawn distances remain unsupported. Source template auras, scripts, immunities, extra flags and static behavior beyond the translated client flags remain unsupported. These limits are not evidence that the Source Profile gate passes; S6 owns that gate.

## Scripted creature immunity, Milestone 4 ledger

Decision 6 keeps unsupported scripted immunities disabled. Milestone 4 restores a static immunity
only when a fully translated unconditional spawn rule clears it with certainty. Overlord Mok'Morokk 4500
regains static 0x20, unit flag 0x100, and rule 450003 clears it. His NPC immunity remains disabled.
Every other entry below still omits static 0x20 or 0x40, unit flags 0x100 or 0x200 respectively.
An entry in both lists loses both translations. The full-world manifest still reports 3,407
templates with at least one unsupported immunity, and alliance-single reports 1,022.

Archaedas 2748 uses a C++ AI, so his immunity stays disabled. Arugal 4275 has a spawn rule with
condition 16255, a source GUID condition that the Module cannot express; his immunity also stays
disabled. Overlord Mok'Morokk supplies the tested translated-clear case. The Native creation packet contains
the restored bit (flags 320), followed by a values update clearing it (flags 64). The spawn
transaction commits without immunity, so this changes the packet sequence but creates no lasting
server-side immunity. A real-client frame effect has not been checked. Only four templates have any EventAI immunity clear: 1840, 4275, 4500 and 10992.
The other three fail the unconditional spawn rule. Omitting their immunity can still affect play.

Creature mana is carried by neither World Source import. Both spawn with zero power and maximum power; source mana pools and mana multipliers remain unsupported.



The spell catalogue reports the same findings in both profiles. Source scripts affect 286 selected
spell entries. The `spells.script` finding lists those entries. `spells.modifier-high-mask` lists
34 effect slots whose source mask exceeds the Module's 32-bit modifier parameter. The low mask
bits retain their existing meaning; high-bit matching and override-class-script behavior remain
unsupported. S5d implements coefficients and minimum target level; two custom flags remain held as described below.

The full Base Snapshot includes the core synthetic effect at slot 3 on spell 21082. Datascripts
can load the Snapshot and author other spells. Opening spell 21082 is refused because the Package
API permits only slots 0 through 2. The baseline Snapshot parser failed on this row before any
Datascript ran; S5b confines the Refusal to that spell without changing Package Identifier Ranges.

Spell metadata has two inactive learn links, `17002:24867` and `24866:24864`. The Module has no
activation flag on a learn link, so it retains them and reports `spellmeta.inactive-learn`.
The source ability link `1515:2997` names a spell absent from the selected spell catalogue. The
import omits that rank link and reports `spellmeta.missing-rank-spell`. Both profiles have these
same findings. The selected proc overlays have no conflicting active-effect masks. A future row
with distinct active masks would remain unloaded and report `spellmeta.proc-mask`, because the
Module stores one family mask per spell.

S5d implements the extra spell columns. `spells.custom-flags` reports 47 selected spells in each
profile. Seventeen use `SEND_CHANNEL_VISUAL`, bit 0x800, which needs a SpellVisual channel-kit
catalogue and repeating visual delivery. Thirty use `TRIGGER_WEAPON_PROCS`, bit 0x2000, which
needs weapon-enchant and item-on-hit dispatch. These two bits are held under decision 11; all
other defined custom bits have gameplay checks. The catalogue retains the held flags. The
spell-behavior report lists every bit and the tests. The existing script and high-mask findings
remain. Automatic negative-coefficient fallbacks retain the Module's prior formulas.

The six replacement catalogues keep the Module's current column projection. Trigger geometry
comes from vmangos, but these extra behaviors have no Module fields. Both profiles select the
complete catalogues and report the same counts.

| Finding | Selected rows | Current limit |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `dbc.trigger-cooldown` | 2 | Trigger cooldowns are not represented. |
| `dbc.trigger-condition` | 0 | A future nonzero source condition will be reported; trigger entry has no condition Gate. |
| `dbc.trigger-script-id` | 2 | Source trigger script lists await the script system. |
| `dbc.trigger-script-name` | 53 | Source named trigger scripts are unsupported. |

The Map catalogue stores vmangos player limits, reset delays and ghost entrances. The Module
still uses its current Instance admission, reset and ghost-routing rules. `dbc.map-player-limit`,
`dbc.map-reset-delay` and `dbc.map-ghost-entrance` report nondefault source values whose gameplay
meaning is not implemented. The current pin has 30 limits, seven reset delays and 25 valid ghost entrances. Named map scripts remain unsupported on 24 maps, reported as `dbc.map-script-name`. Raid lockouts remain tracked in issue #533. The client supplies only
`internal_name`, the archive directory. This is the named Map exception to decision 11.


## EventAI and scripts, Milestone 4

The [full-world census](census/creature-ai.md) and
[alliance-single census](census/creature-ai-alliance-single.md) report every finding code and count.
The [approved sets](approved-sets-m4.md) document the gate. Approval classifies source values;
it does not promise that each command, condition or target can run in the Module.

Full-world emits 4,923 of 6,179 source events. It excludes 310 rows whose template does not use
EventAI and drops 946 unsupported rules. The importer drops the complete rule on its first
unsupported command, target, condition or dependency. The following grouped counts describe
that first refusal, not the number of every unsupported command in the source.

| Finding group | Full-world rules | Alliance-single rules |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `eventai.command` | 467 | 107 |
| `eventai.command-condition` | 51 | 11 |
| `eventai.condition` | 213 | 59 |
| `eventai.encounter` | 69 | 1 |
| `eventai.event` | 75 | 10 |
| `eventai.script` | 48 | 25 |
| `eventai.start-script-source-target-swap` | 2 | 0 |
| `eventai.target` | 28 | 0 |

The Module cannot express the refused per-command conditions, source/target swaps, several
friend and map-event selectors, summons with flags, limits or scripts, movement modes,
instance special states or field mutations.
Of 197 source summon commands, 154 have supported plain shapes, including all 139 plain
opponent-target summons from the review. The emitted full-world rules contain 149 commands. The census lists all 197 by script and step;
the former 157 total incorrectly accepted three target-10 commands in script 1128901.

43 shapes remain refused and five otherwise supported commands do not survive rule admission
or scope. Mor Grayhoof and Isalien triggers, Crystal Fang, the Defias Dockmaster and Shy-Rotam
emit summons. Sethir 6909 retains no translated rule: its summons require uniqueness limits,
radius searches and summon flags. Thor 523 and Dungar Longdrink 352 retain their speech and
both gryphon summons. The Module's summon corpse lifetime differs for source modes 1/4;
`eventai.summon-corpse-lifetime` identifies 84 full-world rules and 17 alliance-single rules.

Twenty of 21 random-emote commands appear in the emitted program. All 93 targeted-emote rows
at this pin remain refused (the review counted 92). Source targeted emotes pause movement,
face the target, delay the animation and restore orientation; a target GUID alone does not
implement that sequence.

These refusals do not substitute a nearby unit or another target. Generic-script refusal reasons
and unreachable script ids remain in the local Compatibility Manifest.

The translated flee command emits broadcast 1150 only when fleeing succeeds and retains the Module's fixed ten-second flight. The source controls
its duration through different movement state. `eventai.flee-fixed-duration` reports 1,563
full-world rules and the alliance count shown in its census. This limitation is explicit.

| Script table | Source rows | Source keys | Emitted keys, full-world | Unsupported keys |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `creature_movement_scripts` | 1788 | 729 | 0 | 729 |
| `event_scripts` | 379 | 119 | 0 | 119 |
| `gameobject_scripts` | 139 | 77 | 0 | 77 |
| `generic_scripts` | 3057 | 701 | 32 | 669 |
| `gossip_scripts` | 522 | 380 | 0 | 380 |
| `quest_end_scripts` | 1696 | 224 | 0 | 224 |
| `quest_start_scripts` | 666 | 99 | 0 | 99 |

Only `generic_scripts` has translated roots through EventAI START_SCRIPT 39. The six other
families have no classic importer dispatcher. vmangos quest-end mail already comes from quest
columns. `gameobject_scripts` keys are spawn GUIDs, confirmed in `GameObject::Use` at the pinned
source commit. No entry-key substitution is made.

Of 176 full-world event-credit candidates, 2460 has emitted credit, 2608 retains its classic
event gate without a working grant, and 174 use their normal imported objectives. The
[event-credit ledger](event-credit-m4.md) lists each outcome and source reference. The 174
fallbacks comprise 11 refused SQL sequences, 61 scripts without dispatch, 39 C++ spell effects,
60 C++ script references and three unresolved grant sources, 3366, 6847 and 6848.

Quest 2460 translates incomplete-quest condition 806 and command 7's 20-yard credit limit.
Quest 2608 is a known completion regression against classic. Its condition 3694 and chat
requests translate, but its scene is refused before it can emit command 7 at 33 seconds.
Persistent emote state 69 and clearing state 0 need a durable animation field and client updates.
The move at 4 seconds is relative to the player; moves at 14, 20 and 30 seconds need the source's
point-movement controller, movement options and final orientation. These systems are absent.
Accepting or flexing cannot complete this quest. Quests 6001 and 6002 still need gossip dispatch.

A dwarf hunter accepted quest 6085, received its Taming Rod, returned the rod, and accepted
Training the Beast 6086 using actual imported rows and Native packets. This verifies the normal
objective fallback. Casting the rod still deletes it, so that path cannot then return it; the same
failure occurs on pre-fix Core 928e3489. The item-use code is unchanged from base 95396fa2 and also
ignores the supplied target. These existing item-use defects are outside the event-gate change.
The reward importer refuses the three-spell wrapper 1579, so Tame Beast is not learned. The
source's C++ taming aura callback is also unimplemented. This is not a verified taming sequence.

Quests 8353-8360 use creature-objective credit, not those event requirements. All eight passed
wrong-emote and correct-emote checks with their actual imported NPC rules and replies on a
Disposable Host. Quest acceptance was staged for these checks; acceptance and reward flows were
not tested. Female and genderless models now select nonempty female broadcast text with male
fallback. Missing gender metadata is reported for three full-world templates. Alternate-gender
model choice remains unsupported; no nonzero alternative was observed at this pin.

VanCleef's aggro and health-threshold yells, voice sounds and two attacking Blackguards passed
against actual imported rows. His player-kill yell is imported but was not exercised. Guardian
creator-GUID and creator-spell client fields are not represented. Zone-wide voice reaches the
same zone on maps 0/1 and the same map and instance elsewhere, matching the pinned source.
Dead creatures can deliver death yells; dead players remain unable to speak.

Rajaxx's aggro and death rules emit the named Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj encounter notification.
His kill yell, map-1 spawn line, map-509 spawn faction and evade yell translate. Map conditions
use source type 33; type 15 is level and remains refused. The classic spawn projection remains
limited to classic definitions. His enrage spell and emote also translate. The encounter translator
uses vmangos instance field ids and states. It
maps source state 0 to reset, and refuses classic field aliases, unrelated special states
and entries whose source spawn maps exclude the bound instance map. Alternative spawn choices
participate in that check. Rajaxx may also spawn on map 1;
his encounter notifications are eligible only in a map-509 instance. A translated encounter notification does not install a Package encounter handler.
The missing handlers and additional source C++ encounter effects remain unsupported.

The source's five EventAI display commands request explicit display ids. Four belong to active
EventAI templates and are refused; the fifth belongs to an excluded AI template. None emits a
display-template instruction. Template-based display dependencies are implemented and tested
with authored fixtures. Guardian 636 is included through spell 5200's dependency. Fixture ids
5,099,000 through 5,099,999 are refused for subjects, broadcasts and template dependencies.
The checked source tables contain no ids in that band.

The 17 SEND_CHANNEL_VISUAL spells and 30 TRIGGER_WEAPON_PROCS spells remain held as documented
above. M4 changes neither flag's implementation.

## Creature behavior lost from the imported program

Generated by `importer/scripts/creature-behavior-ledger.py` from the M4 production plans and vmangos `464179081673cfd240f7ffe7f0daf96bca0b5a70`, patch 10. The inputs stay local.

This comparison reports behavior categories present in the previous imported EventAI and its reachable relays but absent from the vmangos program. Source spell lists count as casts. Equal categories do not prove equivalent spells, speech, timing or targets; partial losses within a retained category need later conformance checks. A source script name identifies C++ behavior that this importer does not load. Refusal codes identify dropped rules, without asserting that they implement every missing classic action.

Deadmines marks content with a playable Package. Other Instance populations do not imply playable encounters. The Alliance marker means the previous scoped EventAI plan includes the entry. These are static comparisons, not new gameplay verification.
